technical_and_design_decisions: Implement new features as Spring XD modules (source, processor) and extensions to the message bus, following existing XD module conventions.

For U2 (Kafka start offset), add a startOffset deployment property to the Kafka source; on initial deployment use Kafka consumer seek() to the requested offset, and during a running stream rely on the existing offset commit mechanism so progress survives crashes.

For U3 and U4 (partition pre-allocation), replace Kafka consumer group rebalancing with manual partition assignment (KafkaConsumer.assign()) using a deterministic partition distribution computed from the number of module instances/containers and total partitions at stream deployment time.

For U6 (reactor-stream processor), use Project Reactor Flux.window(Duration) to implement time-windowed aggregations, evaluate field paths via SpEL, and compute requested aggregate expressions (min, avg, etc.).
For U7 (microbatching), implement a buffering decorator in source modules that accumulates messages for batchInterval milliseconds and emits them as a batch payload.

For U5 (Spark POC), develop a standalone prototype that bridges Kafka to Spark Streaming and evaluates integration patterns with XD; deliver a design document and prototype code, not production-grade module.
For U8 (performance infra), use infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Ansible) to provision Rackspace VMs, deploy Kafka and XD, and run benchmark scripts.
assumptions: A single experienced Java/Spring developer performs all work; effort is expressed in 8-hour workdays.
The existing Spring XD codebase and build environment are available and extensible; no foundational migration is needed.
The Kafka version in use supports manual partition assignment and seek operations (Kafka 0.9+).

For U2, if a stream is undeployed and redeployed without an explicit start offset, it resumes from the last committed offset; if an explicit start offset is provided, it restarts from that offset (clarifying the TBD in the spec).
The Spark POC is time-boxed to 10 workdays and results in a prototype and design recommendation, not a production-ready module.
Performance testing infrastructure effort covers scripting and configuration only; cloud resource costs and procurement are outside the effort estimate.
Wiki documentation is authored in the existing project wiki and covers configuration and examples for the new modules/features.
